answer.reason: The mutant skips applying route policy defaults. A route-level max_attempts=5 is silently dropped and falls back to the config value 3, even though no request override touched it. That breaks the criterion that request overrides take precedence over router and route defaults while unrelated defaults survive.
answer.test_focus: With route_policy_defaults={"max_attempts": 5} and no call or router override for that field, the test must check that the effective max_attempts is 5, not the config default. It must also check that a call override for a different field leaves this route policy default unchanged.

answer.reason: The mutant drops any provider kwarg supplied on the request if its value is falsy (0, None, False, empty). So an explicit request value like {'custom_kwarg': 0} disappears from kwargs, and it would also fail to replace a router or route default for the same key. This breaks both the override rule and the rule that explicit empty or null values stay distinguishable from omission.
sources: Request-level settings shall override router and route defaults, while an explicitly supplied empty or null value shall remain distinguishable from an omitted override.
Generated combinations preserve omission as distinct from an explicit call value.

answer.test_focus: Give a request provider kwarg a falsy value (0, None or an empty collection) and check that it still appears in effective kwargs and overrides a router or route default of the same key.

answer.reason: The mutant drops the step that merges request-level provider kwargs into the effective kwargs. As a result, a call override such as custom_kwarg is silently lost (the effective kwargs come out as {} instead of {'custom_kwarg': 'value'}). This breaks the requirement that request-level settings override router and route defaults.
answer.test_focus: The test must check that a request-level provider kwarg, both one not listed in CALL_OVERRIDE_FIELDS and one that clashes with a route or router default kwarg, shows up in EffectiveSettings.kwargs with the call value. It must also check that unrelated default kwargs are kept.

answer.reason: The mutant never merges router-level provider kwargs into the effective kwargs, so router defaults are silently lost. The confirmed input shows this: with no request override, {'custom_kwarg': 'test_val'} disappears. That breaks the precedence chain (route < router < request) and the criterion that unrelated defaults survive.
answer.test_focus: Check that router-default kwargs appear in the effective kwargs and override route-default kwargs with the same key. Also check that request kwargs override them while unrelated router kwargs survive.
